Synopsis:
Having discovered the true identity of the Emperor (Balduran), one final confrontation with the Emperor about its manipulation in which we learn of how Balduran came to be the Emperor.

Cluster Contexts:
- WYR_DaisyEmperorBalduran.json: You are facing the Emperor in a final, revealing confrontation after learning his true identity as Balduran. Off‑screen, the party has already gained access to Moonrise Towers (and the Emperor recognizes the player as tadpoled/marked), permitting an intimate mind‑meld in which Balduran shares his memories. In those visions he describes a life as a sea captain who founded Baldur’s Gate, an expedition that led him to an illithid colony where he acquired a tadpole and became enthralled to the elder brain, and Ansur’s desperate efforts to pull him free. Balduran admits Ansur saved him from the hivemind but says he refused to be “cured,” that Ansur tried to kill him in what he viewed as mercy, and he killed Ansur first as an act of self‑preservation—framing those choices as necessary steps on his path to power.
- END_BrainBattle_AD_EnemyEmperor.json: The emperor is now an enemy under the Netherbrain's control. He serves as a central character of the last fight.This AD plays on the Emperor's turn. Extra lines are played once for when the party mindflayer uses Karsus' Compulsion on the crown and when the players are racing to get to the opened portal.
- CAMP_DaisyStelmane_AvD.json: Upon our learning of Stelmane’s murder, we stumble on the Emperor in a dream, reflecting nostalgically on its past life with Stelmane and all that it hopes to reclaim (all part of the mind flayer manipulation).
- INT_EmperorRevealed_AfterOrpheus.json: You are in the gith crèche before a grand portrait of Queen Vlaakith; Lae'zel stands nearby reverent toward Vlaakith and openly hostile to any mention of Orpheus. Off-screen Orpheus has already been subdued—an Emperor who is himself a mind flayer used psionic power to reform Orpheus’s globe of domination and restrain him, then approached the party to speak. The scene reveals the true nature of Daisy, gives some of the Emperor’s backstory (he claims he protects the infected and cannot leave with you), explains the technicality by which Orpheus’s power is currently protecting those infected, and makes clear the Brain is a far larger, highly intelligent threat. You have previously met a young gith named Varrl; depending on earlier choices he may be unharmed and persuadable (able to hand over part of chapter 2), injured (allowing a steal or a heal), or otherwise affected by your actions. The party may also face the possibility of transforming into a half‑illithid.
- INT_EmperorRevealed_EmperorPlea.json: You are in the Astral plane amid a pitched fight: Orpheus’ royal guards are engaged with the Emperor (a psionic mind flayer) and swarms of intellect devourers. The Emperor has been trying to recreate a globe of domination to subdue Orpheus—Orpheus is currently chained and apparently controlled when the globe forms, and he seems to “wake” if that control fails. Off‑screen, the player has already been drawn into this conflict and may have previously allied with or opposed the Emperor, so the Emperor’s lines swing between pleading “I am your ally”/“We are in danger” and bitter accusation (“You betrayed me”) depending on the player’s choices. If you side with the Emperor you fight the githyanki with his aid; if you side with the githyanki the Emperor will punish or teleport you back to the Material Plane, forcing a rushed re-entry through the portal while githyanki attack.
